Town of Corte Madera
To maintain rapid 9-1-1 emergency response times and preserve the number of on-duty paramedics ready to respond to accidents/medical emergencies, shall the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority measure be adopted continuing for four years the paramedic services special tax of up to $94.50/ residential living unit or 1,000 square feet of developed nonresidential property, adjusted up to $7. 75/year, generating approximately $786,000 annually, with annual audits, public spending disclosure and all funds for local paramedic services?
YES NO
Votes required to pass: 2/3 voter approval.
Full text of Measure Q

OFFICIAL IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS
Impartial analysis by Town Attorney of Measure Q
ANALYSIS BY THE TOWN ATTORNEY FOR THE TOWN OF CORTE MADERA OF THE TOWN OF CORTE MADERA’S CONTINUATION OF A SPECIAL PARCEL TAX MEASURE FOR PARAMEDIC AND/OR EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES
Measure Q (“Measure”), a Town of Corte Madera (“Town”) special parcel tax measure, seeks voter approval to continue the Town’s levy of a four-year special parcel tax, beginning ten (10) days after the vote is declared by the Town Council, at the following rates:
(1) Nonresidential uses: Ninety-four dollars and fifty cents ($94.50 to a maximum of $117.75) per year for each 1,000 square feet of floor area; (2) Residential Units: Ninety-four dollars and fifty cents ($94.50 to a maximum of $117.75) per year for each residential unit.
The Town estimates the parcel tax, if passed, will provide approximately $786,000 annually. The Town will use the revenue only for the purposes listed in the Measure, which are specifically and solely for the purpose of providing paramedic and/or emergency medical services. This limitation on the use of the proceeds shall be legally binding and enforceable.
If passed, as of ten (10) days after the vote is declared by the Town Council, the parcel tax will supersede and replace the existing parcel tax passed in 2022. If the measure fails, the existing parcel tax would continue until June 30, 2027, when it will cease to be in effect.
The Measure contains certain accountability provisions, including that the Town Treasurer shall prepare and file with the Town Council a report by August 1st of each year stating: (a) the amounts collected and spent by the Town in the previous fiscal year, (b) the status of services authorized to be funded by the proceeds of the tax, and (c) the funds carried over from previous years and to be carried over to future years. Such report shall be available for inspection without charge to any property owner in the Town.
The Town has the authority to levy special taxes upon approval by two-thirds of the votes cast on the special tax proposal. (Cal. Const. art. XIII A, § 4; art. XIII C, § 2; Cal. Gov’t Code §§ 50075-50077, 50079, & 53722.) If two-thirds of the qualified electors voting on this Measure do not vote for approval, it will fail, and the Town will not be authorized to levy the special parcel tax.
This Measure is placed on the ballot by the Town Council.
s/RICHARD D. PIO RODA
Town Attorney

OFFICIAL IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS
Impartial analysis by Town Attorney of Measure R
Town of Fairfax
MEASURE EXTENDING A SPECIAL PARCEL TAX FOR FOUR (4) YEARS AND INCREASING ITS RATE TO FUND LOCAL PARAMEDIC AND PRE-HOSPITAL EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES PROVIDED BY THE ROSS VALLEY PARAMEDIC AUTHORITY
The Town of Fairfax is a member of the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority, a joint powers authority formed to provide paramedic and pre-hospital emergency medical services throughout its member agencies’ boundaries (the “RVPA”).
Under Measure “F”, passed by Fairfax voters in November, 2022, the Town currently levies an annual parcel tax at a rate of $103.50 per taxable residential unit and $103.50 per 1,500 square feet of taxable non-residential floor area. The tax started collection on July 1, 2023 and will expire June 30, 2027, unless extended by voters. Measure “F” funds must be spent on paramedic and pre-hospital emergency medical services provided by the RVPA.
On July 1, 2026, the Town Council placed Measure “R” on the November 3, 2026 General Municipal Election ballot. If approved by two-thirds (2/3) of Fairfax voters, Measure “R” would extend the parcel tax for four (4) years, with a new expiration date of June 30, 2031. It would also increase the tax rates to the following:
For non-residential uses: For each 1,000 square feet of floor area, up to:
$107.50 for fiscal year 2027–2028;
$111.00 for fiscal year 2028–2029;
$114.50 for fiscal year 2029–2030;
$118.00 for fiscal year 2030–2031.
For each residential unit, up to:
$107.50 for fiscal year 2027–2028;
$111.00 for fiscal year 2028–2029;
$114.50 for fiscal year 2029–2030;
$118.00 for fiscal year 2030–2031.
The tax is estimated to generate $432,000 annually until it expires. Measure “R” does not change the purposes of the parcel tax. Tax revenues will continue to be deposited into a special Town fund and used solely for funding paramedic and/or pre-hospital emergency medical services provided through the RVPA.
Measure “R” requires the Town’s Treasurer to file an annual report with the Town Council showing (i) the amount of tax revenues collected and spent by the Town in the previous fiscal year (ii) the status of services funded with tax revenues, and (iii) the funds carried over from previous years and into future years. The report shall be available for inspection without charge to any property owner in the Town.
This parcel tax would be collected in the same time and manner and subject to the same requirements as other property taxes fixed and collected by the County of Marin on behalf of the Town of Fairfax.
A “yes” vote on Measure “R” will approve this parcel tax.
A “no” vote on Measure “R” will not approve this parcel tax.
The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure “R”. If you desire a copy of the Measure, please call the Town’s elections official at (415) 458-2343 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you.
s/JANET COLESON
Town Attorney

OFFICIAL IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS
Impartial analysis by Town Attorney of Measure R
Town of Fairfax
MEASURE EXTENDING A SPECIAL PARCEL TAX FOR FOUR (4) YEARS AND INCREASING ITS RATE TO FUND LOCAL PARAMEDIC AND PRE-HOSPITAL EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES PROVIDED BY THE ROSS VALLEY PARAMEDIC AUTHORITY
The Town of Fairfax is a member of the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority, a joint powers authority formed to provide paramedic and pre-hospital emergency medical services throughout its member agencies’ boundaries (the “RVPA”).
Under Measure “F”, passed by Fairfax voters in November, 2022, the Town currently levies an annual parcel tax at a rate of $103.50 per taxable residential unit and $103.50 per 1,500 square feet of taxable non-residential floor area. The tax started collection on July 1, 2023 and will expire June 30, 2027, unless extended by voters. Measure “F” funds must be spent on paramedic and pre-hospital emergency medical services provided by the RVPA.
On July 1, 2026, the Town Council placed Measure “R” on the November 3, 2026 General Municipal Election ballot. If approved by two-thirds (2/3) of Fairfax voters, Measure “R” would extend the parcel tax for four (4) years, with a new expiration date of June 30, 2031. It would also increase the tax rates to the following:
For non-residential uses: For each 1,000 square feet of floor area, up to:
$107.50 for fiscal year 2027–2028;
$111.00 for fiscal year 2028–2029;
$114.50 for fiscal year 2029–2030;
$118.00 for fiscal year 2030–2031.
For each residential unit, up to:
$107.50 for fiscal year 2027–2028;
$111.00 for fiscal year 2028–2029;
$114.50 for fiscal year 2029–2030;
$118.00 for fiscal year 2030–2031.
The tax is estimated to generate $432,000 annually until it expires. Measure “R” does not change the purposes of the parcel tax. Tax revenues will continue to be deposited into a special Town fund and used solely for funding paramedic and/or pre-hospital emergency medical services provided through the RVPA.
Measure “R” requires the Town’s Treasurer to file an annual report with the Town Council showing (i) the amount of tax revenues collected and spent by the Town in the previous fiscal year (ii) the status of services funded with tax revenues, and (iii) the funds carried over from previous years and into future years. The report shall be available for inspection without charge to any property owner in the Town.
This parcel tax would be collected in the same time and manner and subject to the same requirements as other property taxes fixed and collected by the County of Marin on behalf of the Town of Fairfax.
A “yes” vote on Measure “R” will approve this parcel tax.
A “no” vote on Measure “R” will not approve this parcel tax.
The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure “R”. If you desire a copy of the Measure, please call the Town’s elections official at (415) 458-2343 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you.
s/JANET COLESON
Town Attorney

OFFICIAL IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS
Impartial analysis by City Attorney of Measure S
City of Larkspur
The City Council of the City of Larkspur placed Measure S on the November 3, 2026 ballot to ask voters to extend the existing special parcel tax for paramedic services (“tax” or “Paramedic Tax”) for an additional 4 years. The tax funds services provided by the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority (“Authority”) and will expire on June 30, 2027, unless extended by the voters.
In 1983, the voters of Larkspur, along with the other voters within the boundaries of the Authority, initially approved the Paramedic Tax. Voters have approved extensions and increases in the Paramedic Tax since that time. The Paramedic Tax was last approved by voters in 2022. The current rate of the tax is $103.50 for each residential living unit and for each 1,500 square feet of non-residential developed space, which includes a $0.50 Marin County administrative fee.
Measure S would authorize continuing the Paramedic Tax for another 4 years, until 2031, when it would again have to be renewed by the voters. The Measure would set the rate for the 2027-28 tax year at $107.50 for each taxable living unit and for each 1,000 square feet of non-residential developed space, which would continue to include the $0.50 County administrative fee. It would authorize annual increases of $3.50, with a maximum rate in the fourth year of $118.
As a special tax, the Paramedic Tax is restricted to funding paramedic services, including but not limited to emergency response, training, costs of medical supplies and equipment, and replacement of ambulance transport units.
If Measure S were approved, the Paramedic Tax would terminate automatically after four years, unless extended by a subsequent vote of the voters within the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority.
A “Yes” vote is a vote to approve the extension of the Paramedic Tax for four years and authorize annual increases of up to $4, with a maximum rate not to exceed $118 in the fourth year. A “No” vote is a vote against extension of the Paramedic Tax, which will terminate automatically in June 2027 if not extended. Measure S would be approved if it received a two-thirds majority of “Yes” voters. A copy of the resolution approving the tax is included in the Voter Information Guide.
The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure S. If you desire a copy of the measure, please call the City Clerk’s office at (415) 927-5002 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you.

To maintain rapid 9-1-1 emergency response times and preserve the number of on-duty paramedics ready to respond to accidents/medical emergencies, shall the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority measure be adopted continuing for four years the paramedic services special tax of up to $107.50 / residential living unit or 1,000 square feet of developed nonresidential property, adjusted up to $4.00/ year, generating approximately $834,000 annually, with annual audits, public spending disclosure and all funds for local paramedic services?
YES NO
Votes required to pass: 2/3 voter approval.

OFFICIAL IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS
Impartial analysis by City Attorney of Measure S
City of Larkspur
The City Council of the City of Larkspur placed Measure S on the November 3, 2026 ballot to ask voters to extend the existing special parcel tax for paramedic services (“tax” or “Paramedic Tax”) for an additional 4 years. The tax funds services provided by the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority (“Authority”) and will expire on June 30, 2027, unless extended by the voters.
In 1983, the voters of Larkspur, along with the other voters within the boundaries of the Authority, initially approved the Paramedic Tax. Voters have approved extensions and increases in the Paramedic Tax since that time. The Paramedic Tax was last approved by voters in 2022. The current rate of the tax is $103.50 for each residential living unit and for each 1,500 square feet of non-residential developed space, which includes a $0.50 Marin County administrative fee.
Measure S would authorize continuing the Paramedic Tax for another 4 years, until 2031, when it would again have to be renewed by the voters. The Measure would set the rate for the 2027-28 tax year at $107.50 for each taxable living unit and for each 1,000 square feet of non-residential developed space, which would continue to include the $0.50 County administrative fee. It would authorize annual increases of $3.50, with a maximum rate in the fourth year of $118.
As a special tax, the Paramedic Tax is restricted to funding paramedic services, including but not limited to emergency response, training, costs of medical supplies and equipment, and replacement of ambulance transport units.
If Measure S were approved, the Paramedic Tax would terminate automatically after four years, unless extended by a subsequent vote of the voters within the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority.
A “Yes” vote is a vote to approve the extension of the Paramedic Tax for four years and authorize annual increases of up to $4, with a maximum rate not to exceed $118 in the fourth year. A “No” vote is a vote against extension of the Paramedic Tax, which will terminate automatically in June 2027 if not extended. Measure S would be approved if it received a two-thirds majority of “Yes” voters. A copy of the resolution approving the tax is included in the Voter Information Guide.
The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure S. If you desire a copy of the measure, please call the City Clerk’s office at (415) 927-5002 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you.
s/SKY WOODRUFF
City Attorney City of Larkspur
